selection_rationale: NetOpsTraceBench (rX4f7-1) best matches the programme goal of a workflow-centered, reproducible evaluation of verifier-assisted vs one-shot LLM NetOps pipelines; it targets a clear literature gap (workflow/trace benchmarks), is experimentally falsifiable with a paired design, and has high venue relevance and feasible resource estimates given the manifest.
unresolved_uncertainties: Emulator (Mininet) fidelity to production networks and how simulator limitations affect the composite safety metric (external validity).
Sourcing, synthesis, and privacy/sensitivity risk of the 1,200 intent→config mappings (potential researcher bias and disclosure constraints).
Validator implementation correctness and potential conflation of verifier bugs with model failures; need for independent verifier verification and inter-verifier agreement metrics.
Specification and justification of the composite safety-score (component weights, aggregation function) and its sensitivity to weighting choices.
required_repairs_before_preregistration: Specify the exact composite-safety-score formula, component definitions, and preregistered component weights (and plan for sensitivity analysis over weights).
Provide provenance and sourcing rules for intent→config creation: indicate which examples are synthetic vs consented, exclusion rules for sensitive templates, and release/redaction policy.
Include independent validator verification: unit tests, ground-truth comparisons, inter-verifier agreement reporting, and a plan for adjudicating validator vs model disagreement.
Define emulator limitations explicitly and preregister sensitivity analyses (alternative topologies/parameters, and analyses showing metric robustness to emulator assumptions).

Freeze and publish full preregistration artefacts: exact prompts, model versions/identifiers, random seeds, trace schema, baseline one-shot prompts, and the retry policy (all to be included in the preregistration).
